translationRepairs: s0003 Chinese 〈（馮赟附）〉 uses corner brackets as annotation marks; the English sense is only “(With Feng Yun appended)”, so the stray closing 〉 is a punctuation artifact, not meaning.
The same annotation 〈（馮赟附）〉 should not leave a closing 〉 in the literal English; removing it matches the sense without changing the gloss.
Dong Chuan held Dongchuan as military governor; Hongzhao was appointed his deputy.
Dong Zhang held Dongchuan as military governor; Hongzhao was appointed his deputy.
s0007 names 董璋; 璋 is zhāng, so “Dong Zhang” is required and “Dong Chuan” is a wrong reading of the given name.

Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan killed the army supervisor Li Yan. Hongzhao was terrified and begged to return to court, but Dong Chuan refused. Suspicion grew between them—yet Hongzhao treated him openly and without mistrust, and Zhang came to respect him.

Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan killed the army supervisor Li Yan. Hongzhao was terrified and begged to return to court, but Dong Zhang refused. Suspicion grew between them—yet Hongzhao treated him openly and without mistrust, and Zhang came to respect him.
In s0008 the bare 璋 that refuses Hongzhao’s return is the same 董璋; expanding it as “Dong Zhang” is correct, while “Dong Chuan” invents a different name.
Later Dong Chuan sent him to court on official business, and Hongzhao was able to leave.
Later Dong Zhang sent him to court on official business, and Hongzhao was able to leave.
s0009 後璋有軍事 continues the same person 董璋; “Dong Zhang” restores the source name and “Dong Chuan” remains wrong.
Chonghui reached Fengxiang. Hongzhao received him with elaborate courtesy, entertained him at home, and had his household serve the meal.
Chonghui reached Fengxiang. Hongzhao received him with elaborate courtesy, entertained him at home, and had his wife and concubines serve food and drink.
s0013 has 使其妻妾侍飲食; “household” omits 妻妾, and restoring “wife and concubines serve food and drink” matches the Chinese and the sound literal.

Once enthroned, the emperor made Zhao Yinchao Left Remonstrator and Duanming academician; Zhu Mei director of the Bureau of Revenue and direct academician of Military Affairs; Shen Qian commissioner of the Imperial City; Hao commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat; and Yanlang commissioner of the Imperial Estates.

Once enthroned, the emperor made Zhaoyin Left Remonstrator and Duanming academician; Zhuanmei director of the Bureau of Revenue and direct academician of Military Affairs; Shenqian commissioner of the Imperial City; Hao commissioner of the Northern Palace Secretariat; and Yanlang commissioner of the Imperial Estates.

s0049 uses bare given names 昭胤、專美、審虔 (Han Zhaoyin, Li Zhuanmei, Song Shenqian); “Zhao Yinchao”, “Zhu Mei”, and “Shen Qian” are invented full names, and the proposed Zhaoyin/Zhuanmei/Shenqian restores the source forms.

In time Zhao Yinchao and Hao became chief councillors, Yanlang deputy, Shen Qian commander of the palace foot guards, and Xue Wenyu director of Appointments and direct academician of Military Affairs.
In time Zhaoyin and Hao became chief councillors, Yanlang deputy, Shenqian commander of the palace foot guards, and Xue Wenyu director of Appointments and direct academician of Military Affairs.
s0050 again has 昭胤 and 審虔; replacing “Zhao Yinchao” and “Shen Qian” with Zhaoyin and Shenqian corrects the false English names.
Shen Qian held the armies; Zhu Mei and Wenyu shaped policy; Zhao Yinchao, Hao, and Yanlang held the confidential seals.
Shenqian held the armies; Zhuanmei and Wenyu shaped policy; Zhaoyin, Hao, and Yanlang held the confidential seals.
s0051 lists 審虔、專美、昭胤; Shenqian, Zhuanmei, and Zhaoyin are the accurate bare forms, not Shen Qian, Zhu Mei, or Zhao Yinchao.
Yanlang’s faction urged keeping Jingtang in the capital. Zhao Yinchao and Zhu Mei objected: “Jingtang and Zhao Yanshou both married Tang princesses. You cannot hold one and not the other.”
Yanlang’s faction urged keeping Jingtang in the capital. Zhaoyin and Zhuanmei objected: “Jingtang and Zhao Yanshou both married Tang princesses. You cannot hold one and not the other.”
s0054 speakers are 昭胤、專美; “Zhaoyin and Zhuanmei” matches the Chinese, while “Zhao Yinchao and Zhu Mei” invents wrong names.
The emperor plotted with Yanlang day and night. Zhu Mei and Wenyu slept in the Zhongxing Hall and were called in for counsel, often until midnight.
The emperor plotted with Yanlang day and night. Zhuanmei and Wenyu slept in the Zhongxing Hall and were called in for counsel, often until midnight.
s0060 has 專美、文遇; “Zhuanmei” is the correct given name for 專美, and “Zhu Mei” is a false English name.
The emperor read it, flew into a rage, tore the letter apart, and summoned Ma Yinsun to answer: “Revile him in the vilest terms.”.
The emperor read it, flew into a rage, tore the letter apart, and summoned Ma Yinsun to answer: “Revile him in the vilest terms.”
s0075 ends the quoted order at 「宜以惡語詆之。」; the English needs one closing quote and no trailing period after it.
The emperor received the letter, was furious, tore it apart with his hands and cast it away, and summoned the academician Ma Yinsun to draft a reply, saying: “Use harsh words to revile him.”.
The emperor received the letter, was furious, tore it apart with his hands and cast it away, and summoned the academician Ma Yinsun to draft a reply, saying: “Use harsh words to revile him.”
The same s0075 quotation should not carry an extra period after the closing English quotation mark in the literal field.
The emperor said: “I see Wenyu and my flesh crawls—I want to stab him.”.
The emperor said: “I see Wenyu and my flesh crawls—I want to stab him.”
s0081 is a single quoted speech 「我見文遇肉顫，欲抽刀刺之。」; the idiomatic English should end at the closing quote without a following period.
The emperor said: “When I see Wenyu my flesh trembles—I want to draw a knife and stab him.”.
The emperor said: “When I see Wenyu my flesh trembles—I want to draw a knife and stab him.”
The same s0081 speech needs the same quote-final punctuation fix in the literal field.
Song said: “Wenyu is a petty man who has ruined everything. Stabbing him would only shame the throne.”.”
Song said: “Wenyu is a petty man who has ruined everything. Stabbing him would only shame the throne.”
s0082 ends 「…刺之益醜。」 with one closing quote; the duplicated .”.” in English is a transcription error.
Song said: “Wenyu is a petty man who has ruined a great affair. To stab him would only add ugliness.”.”
Song said: “Wenyu is a petty man who has ruined a great affair. To stab him would only add ugliness.”
The same s0082 closing requires one English quotation mark in the literal field, not the duplicated .”.”.
s0087 closes Shenqian’s speech with 不如還也。」; the English should end after the quotation mark without an extra period.
The same s0087 speech-close needs the identical punctuation repair in the literal field.
When Emperor Min took the throne, he made the Deposed Emperor Beijing commissioner without a formal edict and sent palace attendant Zhao Chuyuan to hurry him on his way.
When Emperor Min took the throne, he made the Deposed Emperor Defender of the Northern Capital without a formal edict and sent palace attendant Zhao Chuyuan to hurry him on his way.
In s0185, 北京 is the Later Tang Northern Capital and 留守 is its Defender; the revised wording gives the historical office rather than suggesting a commissioner in modern Beijing.
Emperor Min enthroned Hongshi for killing Congrong. Yicheng’s resentment deepened.
When Emperor Min took the throne, Hongshi often boasted of the merit of killing Congrong, and Yicheng’s resentment deepened.
s0127 湣帝即位，弘實常以誅從榮功自負 says Min took the throne and Hongshi boasted of killing Congrong; “enthroned Hongshi” invents the wrong agent and action.
candidateDispositions: Component of an office recorded in this unit, not a person name.
